card: This draft demonstration PR showcases the complete removal of AssumeUTXO snapshot loading, background historical validation, and multi-chainstate infrastructure across Bitcoin Core. It simplifies validation, downloading, cache allocation, LevelDB ownership, and storage cursors by collapsing ChainstateManager back to a single active chainstate. The author states the PR is not intended for merge, but rather serves as a reference point for smaller proposals to simplify core validation code. The change is motivated by low feature adoption, trust model ambiguities surrounding background validation, and the disproportionate complexity multiple chainstates impose on the most critical parts of the codebase.
changed_since_previous: Rebased after the test fixture coin-insertion cleanup was split out and merged as PR #36601.
evidence: PR description: 'Multiple chainstates affect much more than snapshot loading: ordinary validation changes have to account for different chainstate roles, candidate sets, notifications, downloads, pruning, cache allocation, database lifetimes and locks.'

PR description citing Core Dev meeting: 'there was rough agreement about the ambiguity background validation introduces: we trust a snapshot enough to use it immediately, but describe that trust as temporary until the same node finishes checking history.'

PR description notes adoption lag and IBD improvements: 'adoption isn't where we hoped it would be... Ordinary IBD is also getting faster: #35295 is already merged, and the upcoming pruneassumevalid will make pruned IBD even faster.'
problem: Supporting concurrent chainstates forces pervasive special-casing across block download, cache management, LevelDB lifecycles, indexers, prune heights, wallet rescans, and validation interface notifications. This introduces significant architectural overhead and synchronization complexity into core validation code for a feature that has seen low real-world adoption.

risk.why: A mistake in refactoring core validation, block storage cursors, or chainstate initialization could cause node crashes, chainstate corruption, or consensus desynchronization.

scope_notes: Explicit draft demonstration PR (+539/-5895 across 83 files) not intended for merge as a monolithic change. It illustrates the architectural simplification possible if AssumeUTXO is partially or completely removed, serving as a reference for smaller incremental PRs.
summary: Removes AssumeUTXO snapshot loading (loadtxoutset), background historical sync, and multi-chainstate infrastructure across Bitcoin Core. Collapses ChainstateManager, block downloading, cache sizing, pruning bounds, and block storage cursors back down to a single active chainstate. Coins databases are owned directly by value instead of being dynamically reopened, and datadirs with active snapshot markers are rejected at startup while retaining dumptxoutset exports and ordinary assumevalid validation.
